page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading. The processor operates at 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core, and includes 3780 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory and processing capabilities. It achieves a cached read-only memory bandwidth of 1171.61 GB/sec and an uncached large-block write speed of 57.42 GB/sec. Compute performance is highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11346.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 25302.46. The hardware-accelerated instruction sets support efficient cryptography and data processing, yielding a Passmark encryption test score of 16008.41 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 28.73 GB/sec. For database workloads, it handles 21.05 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 8547.62 in Passmark database operations.

Given its massive memory footprint relative to the vCPU count, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications. The inclusion of 3780 GB of local storage makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring large, high-speed local scratch space without the overhead of external storage. It is well-suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The Intel AMX extensions also enable moderate local machine learning tasks, as evidenced by a prompt processing speed of 107.84 tokens/sec on a medium 7B LLM model.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It configures 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 512.0 GB of RAM and 3780 GB of local storage. This hardware profile delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core, backed by a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks show robust performance, including a cached memory read bandwidth of 1171.61 GB/sec, 21.05 million Redis SET operations per second, and a Passmark database score of 8547.62. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it relies on its high-capacity memory and fast local storage to excel in memory-intensive workloads. This makes the server highly efficient for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data analytics pipelines.
